title: The five risk steps woven into iterations
blurb: Name the five risk steps, say what happens in each, and place them in the rhythm of planning sessions, retrospectives and iterations.
question: A delivery team gathers and documents new threats at the start of every iteration planning session. Which step of the risk technique is the team carrying out?

teach.h: Risk in agile: same purpose, new rhythm
teach.body: The risk practice exists to identify, assess and control uncertainties that could affect the project's objectives, so the chance of success improves. PRINCE2 Agile keeps that purpose and adapts the familiar five-step technique: identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate. What changes is the timing. Instead of a separate risk meeting cycle, the steps ride on events the team already holds: planning sessions, retrospectives and the iteration loop itself.

teach.h: What each step means in agile
head: Step
What happens
Where it lives
teach.caption: Book reference: 10.3.1, Figure 10.1.

teach.h: Identify: a fixed agenda item, not an occasional event
teach.body: The book suggests that identifying risks is a fixed part of every planning session and of team and project retrospectives, where risks are gathered and documented. Risks can still surface anywhere: in a stand-up, a demo or any workshop. The point is that there is a guaranteed, regular moment in each iteration when the team deliberately looks for new threats and opportunities.

The last two steps are not separate events. Implementing responses is part of the continuous iteration cycles: a mitigation action is done like any other piece of work. Communicating is built into the communication procedures and feedback loops already in place, such as dashboards, workshops and demos. So in every iteration and every stage, risk work is happening alongside delivery rather than after it.

rows.label: Question
values: What will we do about it?

teach.body: Project manager Aisha Bello is running an agile project to move the council's parking permits online. In the iteration planning session, product owner Gareth Lloyd's team lists a new threat: the payment provider may change its interface. They estimate its likelihood and impact (assess), then add a response story to build a test harness (plan). The story is built in the iteration (implement), and the team dashboard shows its status (communicate). At the retrospective they look for new risks again.

teach.text: Do not move risk identification to the progress review or the project closure workshop. Risks can come up anywhere, but the book's fixed home for identifying them is every planning session and every team and project retrospective.

items: Risk practice purpose: identify, assess and control uncertainties to improve the chance of success.
Five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate (10.3.1, Figure 10.1).
Identify: a fixed part of every planning session and team and project retrospective.
Assess: estimate and evaluate. Plan: plan the risk responses.
Implement and communicate: inside the continuous iteration cycles and existing feedback loops.

summary: You can now name the five risk steps and say what each one does. You can also place them in the agile rhythm: identification in planning sessions and retrospectives, implementation and communication inside the iteration cycle.

A.q: Which sequence shows the five steps of the risk technique that PRINCE2 Agile adapts?
A.why: PRINCE2 Agile recommends adapting the five-step technique: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate (10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

whyNot.1: Capture, assess, recommend, decide, implement is the issues technique, not the risk technique.
whyNot.2: This is not a PRINCE2 sequence; escalation is part of controlling a stage, not a risk step.
whyNot.3: Plan, do, check, act is a general improvement cycle, not the PRINCE2 risk technique.

A.q: In which step are risks estimated and evaluated?
A.why: In the assess step, risks are estimated and evaluated (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Identify is where risks are gathered and documented.
whyNot.1: Plan is where the risk responses are planned.
whyNot.3: Implement is where the planned responses are carried out.

A.q: Where does the book suggest risk identification should be a fixed part of the agenda?
options: Each project closure workshop and lessons report
Each planning session and team or project retrospective
Each progress review workshop and highlight report
Each project canvas workshop and stage boundary
A.why: Identification is suggested as a fixed part of every planning session and of team and project retrospectives, where risks are gathered and documented (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Closure looks back at lessons; risks can be raised there but it is not the fixed home of identification.
whyNot.2: The progress review assesses status and celebrates achievements; it is not where identification is fixed.
whyNot.3: The canvas workshop has a risk analysis topic, but it happens once in starting up, not each iteration.

B.q: A team has agreed what it will do to reduce a supplier risk. In which step does carrying out that action fall?
B.why: Carrying out planned responses is the implement step, which is part of the continuous iteration cycles (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Assess estimates and evaluates the risk; it does not carry out responses.
whyNot.1: Communicate shares risk status through existing feedback loops.

B.q:
Which two statements about the risk steps in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. Implement and communicate are part of the continuous iteration cycles and feedback loops.
2. Risks are identified once, in the initiation stage, and then monitored.
3. Plan is the step in which risk responses are planned.
4. Assess is the step in which risks are gathered and documented.
B.why: Implement and communicate are woven into the iteration cycles and communication loops (1), and plan is where responses are planned (3) (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: identification is part of every planning session and retrospective.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: identification recurs, and gathering and documenting risks is the identify step.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: assess estimates and evaluates; gathering and documenting is identify.

B.q: What is the purpose of the risk practice?
options: To control changes to the project's baseline
To monitor actual achievement against the plan
To identify, assess and control uncertainties
To define the users' requirements of the products
B.why: The risk practice identifies, assesses and controls uncertainties that would affect objectives, improving the chance of success (10.1).

whyNot.0: Controlling changes to the baseline is the purpose of the issues practice.
whyNot.1: Comparing achievement against plans is the purpose of the progress practice.
whyNot.3: Documenting user requirements and how they will be met is the quality practice.

C.q: During a retrospective, a team lists two new risks and then rates how likely and how serious each one is. Which two steps has it carried out?
C.why: Listing and documenting risks is identify; rating likelihood and impact is assess (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: No responses were planned, so the plan step has not happened yet.
whyNot.2: Nothing has been carried out, so implement has not happened.
whyNot.3: The team has neither planned responses nor shared risk status.

C.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile handle the implement and communicate steps of the risk technique?
options: As a monthly risk meeting chaired by project assurance
As tasks owned by project support after each stage
As actions held back until an exception report is raised
As part of the iteration cycles and existing feedback loops
C.why: Implement and communicate are part of the continuous iteration cycles and the established communication procedures and feedback loops (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: No separate monthly risk meeting is prescribed; the steps ride on the iteration rhythm.
whyNot.1: Project support may help administer risk, but the steps happen within each iteration, not after each stage.
whyNot.2: Risk responses are carried out as normal work; an exception report is for forecast tolerance breaches.

C.q: A tester raises a new risk during a daily stand-up. What does this show about risk identification in agile?
options: Risks can surface at any time, though planning and retrospectives give a fixed slot
Risks raised at a stand-up go straight to the project board as an exception report
Risks belong to the agile enablement workshop and must wait until it is next held
Risks raised after initiation are recorded as issues in the issue register instead
C.why: Risks can be identified at any time; the book suggests planning sessions and retrospectives as the fixed, regular point for identification (10.3.1).

whyNot.1: An exception is for a forecast breach of tolerance, not for every new risk.
whyNot.2: The agile enablement workshop reviews agile-adoption risks for the board; team risks are not held back for it.
whyNot.3: A risk is an uncertain event whenever it is raised; it does not become an issue because of when it was spotted.

reteach.title: The weekly shop
reteach.question: How is managing risk in agile like planning a household's weekly shop?

blocks.body: Each week you check the cupboard for what might run out (identify) and judge how soon and how badly (assess). You write the list (plan), buy and stock up during the week (implement) and tell the household what is on the shelf (communicate). Because you do this every week, nothing builds up unnoticed. PRINCE2 Agile does the same at every planning session and retrospective.

blocks.text: Gathering and documenting = identify. Estimating and evaluating = assess. Deciding responses = plan. Keep those three apart.

explain.body: PRINCE2 Agile adapts the PRINCE2 risk technique of five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate.

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In the risk technique, the [?] step is where risk responses are planned.
test.why: The plan step is addressed by planning the necessary risk responses (10.3.1).

whyNot.2: Implement carries out the responses already planned.

explain.body: Identification is suggested as a fixed part of every planning session and every team and project retrospective, where risks are gathered and documented.

test.q: Which event is a fixed home for identifying risks in PRINCE2 Agile?
test.why: Risk identification is a fixed part of every planning session and retrospective (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Risks can be noted at closure, but it is not the regular home of identification.
whyNot.2: Updating the release map is a planning activity in the plans practice.
whyNot.3: The end project report reviews performance; it is not where risks are identified.

explain.body: Once identified, risks are estimated and evaluated: how likely they are and how big their effect would be.

test.q: A team scores each newly listed risk for probability and impact. Which step is this?
test.why: Estimating and evaluating risks is the assess step (10.3.1).

whyNot.1: Communicate shares risk status; it does not score risks.
whyNot.2: Identify gathers and documents risks before they are scored.
whyNot.3: Plan decides the responses after the risks are assessed.

explain.body: These two steps are part of the continuous iteration cycles and the established communication procedures and feedback loops, so they happen in every iteration and stage.

test.q: Where do the implement and communicate steps take place in an agile project?
options: In a separate risk review held at the end of each stage
In the board's regular agile enablement workshops
In the continuous iteration cycles and feedback loops
In the initiation stage, before any delivery work begins
test.why: Implement and communicate are part of the continuous iteration cycles and established communication procedures and feedback loops (10.3.1).

whyNot.0: No separate stage-end risk review is needed; the steps run within each iteration.
whyNot.1: The agile enablement workshop reviews agile-adoption risks; it does not carry out every response.
whyNot.3: Responses are carried out throughout delivery, not just before it starts.
